major_reasons: Many reviews were polished, generic, and template-like
Comments covered rubric-style dimensions instead of lived experiences
Concrete course-specific details were sparse or superficial
Some entries were invalid placeholders like "nan"
recurring_artifacts: Trailing fragments like "Feedback," "Still," or single-word cutoffs
Balanced pros/cons structure repeated across reviews
Checklist sequencing of topics: pacing, tooling, feedback, collaboration, grading
Repeated generic phrases about workload, rubrics, LMS, and study groups
realism_mismatches: Specific course names/instructors paired with interchangeable complaints
Supposedly personal reviews lacked named assignments, policies, or distinctive incidents
Tone was unusually polished and uniform for casual student feedback
Some text referenced style/tone itself rather than the class experience
Malformed openings/closings and placeholder tokens do not match authentic submissions
prompt_edit_suggestions: Require fully complete reviews with explicit ending checks
Ask for 2-3 concrete course-specific details or incidents
Ban placeholder/null outputs and validate non-empty text
Reduce rubric/checklist prompting that encourages category-by-category coverage
Prefer natural first-person reflection over evenly balanced summary prose
summary: Judge suspicion centered on truncation artifacts, generic over-polished language, formulaic balanced structure, weak course-specific grounding, and occasional malformed/missing outputs.
